newsitem.title: UK: Lead market direction depends on China - Billiton.
newsitem.headline: Lead market direction depends on China - Billiton.

text.p: The direction of the lead market for the rest of 1996 and going into 1997 will depend on the activity of the Chinese, the latest weekly report of Billiton Metals Ltd said.
In recent years China's lead production has risen faster than its consumption and as a result it has become by far the major exporter of refined metal to the West.
This year's exports could exceed the peak year of 1994 when China's exports reached 172,000 tonnes, Billiton said.
There was a marked surge during the third quarter and the rise in London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks during August resulted from the delivery of Chinese material into Singapore warehouses.
But Chinese exports may have fallen from peak levels, and should they fail to pick up the lead market has the potential to tighten considerably in the months ahead, Billiton said.
As producer stocks are at relatively low levels, after a third quarter decline, we could see a resumption of the drawdown in LME stocks.
As 1997 progresses the lead market will move gradually from deficit to surplus and prices will peak in the first half of the year, Billiton said.
